title: elastic-latency-sla-subsidy-roughs
body:
Goal: sketch a compact heuristic for pricing a latency-sensitive SLA/subsidy for interactive apps (chat, copilots) — think: per-active-user uplift + per-token baseline. Quick hack for discussion: 'latency premium' = amortized infra delta for hitting X ms p95 across load profile, plus margin.

Context & motivation:
- A lot of customers want <200ms p95 for 1–10k DAUs; achieving that costs us non-linear infra (reserved GPUs, more replication, less batching).
- Hosted PAYG + reserved capacity products muddy the signal; want a simple add-on for self-serve/prospecting: e.g., +% on top of token price or an additive per-active-user fee.

Assumptions (back of envelope numbers, tweakable):
- Target SLOs considered: 200ms p95 (gold), 400ms p95 (silver), best-effort (bronze).
- Typical interactive request: 30 tokens input, 70 tokens output => 100 tokens total per turn.
- Average turns per DAU/day for app class = 25 (low-medium engagement), DAUs = 10k for baseline.
- Average concurrency at peak for 10k DAU: 0.4% concurrency => 40 concurrent requests at peak. (this is sensitive)
- GPU efficiency: 80 tokens/sec sustained on our mid-tier GPU for target model/quantization; batching increases throughput but hurts p95.
- Hourly cost per GPU (amortized infra + power + overhead) = $3.50 (hosted blend).

Compute math: how many GPUs needed to support 40 concurrent low-latency sessions if we avoid large batching?
- If we aim for median response latency ~150ms per turn and we process tokens incrementally, effective tokens/sec per concurrent stream ~ (tokens per turn) / latency => 100 tokens / 0.15s ≈ 667 tokens/sec per concurrent user — this is unrealistic because we stream; better to think in sustained throughput needed.
- Simpler model: we bound GPU capacity by concurrent * tokens-per-second-per-session. For streaming-friendly models assume each concurrent session consumes ~6 tokens/sec (small-turn streaming).
- So throughput needed = 40 * 6 = 240 tokens/sec. If one GPU does 80 tokens/sec (for low-latency config), need 3 GPUs (240/80=3). Add 20% headroom = 3.6 -> round to 4 GPUs.
- Cost per hour = 4 * $3.50 = $14/hr -> daily = $336 -> monthly (30d) = $10,080.
- Spread across DAUs (10k) -> raw infra monthly per DAU = $1.008. This is just infra for latency sensitive serving footprint (not storage, KMS, control plane).

Translate to pricing constructs:
Option A — per-active-user uplift:
- Add-on price = infra-per-DAU * markup (say 1.5x) = $1.008 * 1.5 ≈ $1.51 / DAU / month. Round to $1.50.
- Pros: predictable, simple for product teams. Cons: penalizes low-usage DAUs or early-stage apps.

Option B — latency premium on tokens (additive $/k token):
- Monthly tokens consumed by DAU: 25 turns * 100 tokens = 2,500 tokens/day -> 75,000 tokens/month per DAU.
- Infra cost per DAU = $1.008 -> per-1k-tokens uplift = $1.008 / 75 = $0.01344 per 1k tokens (~1.34 cents).
- With markup 1.5x -> ~2 cents per 1k tokens.
- Pros: usage-aligned; Cons: clunky for product integrating multi-channel (embedding heavy).

Option C — concurrent-seat reservation (for customers who want strict SLO):
- Sell 'concurrency seats' of size N (e.g., 10 concurrent slots) priced by GPU-equivalent capacity.
- From above: 1 GPU ~ 80 tokens/sec ~ supports ~13 concurrent sessions (80/6). So 1 seat ~ GPU/13. Pricing: hourly cost for 1 seat = ($3.5/hr) / 13 ≈ $0.27/hr -> monthly ≈ $200/month for continuous reservation per seat.
- Offer monthly packs with discounts: 10-seat pack = $1,700/mo (15% discount), 100-seat enterprise tier.
- Pros: direct mapping to infra; nice for large customers. Cons: complexity for self-serve discovery.

Edge factors & levers (things to model):
- Caching/prefix reuse: conversation-level caching can cut per-turn tokens by ~20–40% for highly templated apps. That reduces needed GPUs or raises effective capacity. We should model cache hit-rate sensitivity (10/20/40%).
- Quantization & model family: smaller models reduce tokens/sec cost by 2–4x; allow cheaper latency tiers.
- Prewarm and tail-latency: prewarmed replica per region increases cost but reduces cold-start tails.
- Scheduling overhead & multitenancy: tenant isolation for SLOs means lower statistical multiplexing -> higher reserved capacity factor.

Risk and behavioral effects:
- Per-DAU charge may push customers to throttle DAUs or claim they’re not 'active' -> need clear active-user definition and instrumentation.
- Token uplift may be gamed by sending longer contexts server-side. Consider combining with per-session concurrency cap.
- Concurrency seats align incentives but require sales conversation; fine for mid-enterprise.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate our tokens/sec/session assumption across 3 reference models (small, mid, large) and three quantization profiles.
- Look up actual blended GPU hourly cost across regions (we used $3.5/hr as placeholder).
- Build a small Monte Carlo model to vary DAU, concurrency%, token-per-turn, cache-hit-rate and output recommended pricing for each option (A/B/C).
- How to present on billing UI: additive line item per-app 'Latency SLA (200ms p95)' OR new product 'Dedicated interactive capacity' with seat concept?

Quick example variants (sensitivity):
- If peak concurrency is 0.8% (instead of 0.4%), GPUs double -> infra-per-DAU ~ $2.0 -> per-DAU price ~ $3 with markup.
- If cache hit-rate 30% -> tokens high-cost portion drop -> effective infra-per-DAU down ~25% -> price ~ $1.1 -> round $1.25.

Notes on UX & enforcement:
- For per-DAU, define 'active' = 5+ turns in 30-day window or simple: any 1-turn in 30-day -> might overcharge. Consider 7-day active window.
- For token uplift, annotate invoices with 'Latency premium (2c / 1k tokens) — gold SLA'.
- For concurrency seats, provide dashboard showing seat utilization, recommended resizing.

Final quick proposal (starter):
- Launch experiment: "Gold Latency SLA (200ms p95)" as a paid add-on with two purchase methods: per-active-user ($1.50 / DAU / month) OR token-premium (2c per 1k tokens). For customers >50k DAU, recommend concurrency-seat offers (sales).
- Track adoption, churn signal, and infra delta (measure real GPU hours pinned vs baseline).

Appendix: shorthand formulae to embed in calc sheet later
- GPUs_needed = ceil( (peak_concurrency * DAUs * tokens_per_session_per_sec) / tokens_per_sec_per_GPU * (1 + headroom) )
- infra_per_DAU_month = (GPUs_needed * gpu_hourly_cost * 24 * 30) / DAUs
- per_1k_tokens_uplift = infra_per_DAU_month / (monthly_tokens_per_DAU / 1000)

Quick links/refs (placeholders):
- jira:PRIC-472 (experiment ticket)
- confluence: latency-subsidy design doc (draft)

End of scratchpad — bring to pricing sync with Maya & Liam next Tue.
